text:
Spencer Knight gave Chicago the night it needed. The Blackhawks snapped a three-game winless run (0-3-0) by beating Los Angeles 2-1 at the United Center, and the goalie who stopped 25 of 26 shots was the reason it held. Knight, drafted 13th overall by the Panthers in 2019 and a .931 save percentage man at Boston College before turning pro, was named the game's first star.

Our numbers say he earned it. Expected goals measures the quality of chances, and the shots Knight faced were worth 3.14 of them, so he saved about two goals more than an average goalie would have. Los Angeles opened the scoring on Samuel Helenius's wrist shot 2:31 into the game, a chance with roughly a 23 percent shot at going in. Chicago answered late in the second period when Roman Kantserov, the 2023 second-round pick fresh from 63 KHL games with Metallurg Magnitogorsk, scored on the power play with a snap shot. Wyatt Kaiser then won it early in the third with a wrist shot that was only an 8 percent look. The Blackhawks spent the second period in control, out-chancing LAK 1.83 to 1.02 in expected goals, and Tyler Bertuzzi had a 28 percent chance in the first that Anton Forsberg turned aside.

By shot attempts Chicago led 70 to 59, and our simulation of replays of every shot gives CHI a slim 51 percent deserve-to-win mark against LAK's 49. Forsberg was strong too, saving about a goal more than expected. This was close, and Chicago's goalie was the difference. The Blackhawks leave with the winless run behind them, while the Kings, who went 0 for 3 on the power play, head home with a one-goal loss they had nearly as good a case to avoid.
